bus.name: turn.started
bus.description: Published once per turn when memory takes the user's message as turn `turn` (`TurnMemory.persistMessage`; `Agent.turn` runs it before the host's `use`). `runId` names the run, `userMessage` is what the user said (as the session stored it: its images, inline as base64, normalised), `meta` is the host's metadata the turn was begun with (`{}` when none was given; never shown to the model), and `resumes`, present only on a turn that resumes an earlier one, is that turn's number. Not journaled from the bus: the session stored its own `turn.started` when the turn began, with `meta` and `resumes` only when they were given. A subscription made in `use` never sees it; one in the host's per-turn layer or a session plugin does.

bus.name: step.started
bus.description: Published by the step loop as each step starts. `run` is the run of the turn the step belongs to (0 for the turn's first run, one up for each later `Turn.run`; a record written before runs were counted reads 0), as on `step.ended`, `assistant.message`, `completion.evaluated`, `context.built` and `stream.fallback`: a step is named by its turn, run and step. `planned` is true for step 0 of a host-planned batch, which makes no provider call; `activeTools` are the tool names the step offers the model. Journaled as `step.started`.

bus.name: tool.started
bus.description: Published by the tool registry after admission, and flushed before waiting for execution permits or entering the handler. It proves durable admission, not handler execution: a queued call can still be refused after its breaker trips, or a nested call when permits are occupied. `invocationId` (`<runId>:call:<n>`) pairs it with its `tool.progress`, `tool.completed` or later `tool.refused`; `toolCallId`, when present, is the provider pairing key or the loop's deterministic id; `input` is the decoded parameters; `labels` and `stage` come from the tool's annotations. Initial admission refusals publish only `tool.refused`; `step.ended.results` lists every recorded result, refused calls included. Journaled as `tool.started`, input included.

bus.name: tool.refused
bus.description: Published by the tool registry when it refuses a call before the handler runs: the tool is not active (`inactive`), the turn lacks a permission (`forbidden`), ActionPolicy denied it (`denied`), a legacy turn-wide budget is reached (`call-limit` or the annotation's `tool-call-limit`), the host's per-tool loop-run budget is reached (`run-call-limit`), the loop-run/tool breaker is open (`tripped`), or a nested call would wait on occupied permits (`concurrency`). Initial refusals replace tool.started; a queued breaker recheck or nested permit refusal may follow a durable tool.started admission, with no tool.completed. `toolCallId`, when present, is the provider pairing key or the loop's deterministic id. `invocationId` is minted before the checks and retained on every lifecycle event; `message` is the model's failed result, which step.ended.results lists as not ok. Journaled as tool.refused without input. Stored format 7 adds run-call-limit, tripped and concurrency; earlier journals still decode.

bus.name: tool.progress
bus.description: Published by `publishToolProgress` from inside a tool handler, between that call's `tool.started` and `tool.completed` (same `step`, `invocationId`, optional `toolCallId` and `tool`). `channel` is stdout or stderr for a command's output as it arrives, status for anything else the tool reports; `text` is that output or message. Transient: never journaled; `tool.completed` carries the result.

bus.name: tool.completed
bus.description: Published by the tool registry when a handler returned or failed (`ok`). `toolCallId`, when present, pairs it with the assistant's call and its result. `result` is the decoded value, `encoded` its wire form as the model receives it. `durationMs` runs from just after `tool.started` to the handler's exit, so it includes any wait for the tool's read or write lane. Journaled as `tool.completed` without `input`, `result` and `encoded`: memory keeps the call and its result (`memory.message`, `memory.tool-result`).

bus.name: step.ended
bus.description: Published by the step loop once per step, after the step's tail is recorded and before its completion is evaluated; nothing is recorded under the step after it (the loop's corrective, nudge or steer is the next step's). `status` is how the step's own call, tools and tail came out: completed, failed, cancelled, malformed (a response the model could not form, a tool that does not exist or parameters that do not decode: none of its tool calls ran, the loop answers it with a corrective turn, and the step has no `assistant.message` and no `completion.evaluated`), or truncated (a response cut short: its `assistant.message` carries its finish reason, none of its tool calls ran, each is answered as cut, and the step has no `completion.evaluated`); a completion that fails afterwards fails the run, not the step. `results` are the step's recorded tool results (memory entry, tool call id, tool, ok), in log order, refused calls and a truncated step's cut calls (not ok) included. Journaled as `step.ended` (records with status malformed are not read by 0.14 and older, and records with status truncated, like malformed ones, are not read by releases before stored format 2).

bus.description: Published by the step loop after `step.ended`, with the verdict of the host's completion policy for that step; none after a malformed or truncated step. A verdict that awaits tasks is evaluated again once they finish, publishing a second event. Journaled as `completion.evaluated`.

bus.name: context.built
bus.description: Published before each provider call, once the step's context is built (none for a planned step 0). It carries the memory strategy and its version, the context and system-prompt fingerprints, the token estimate of the messages, the tokens reserved for the system prompt and tool schemas, the run's `budgetTokens` (the whole request's; memory compacted the messages toward `budgetTokens - reservedTokens`), how many compactions the build applied, and the active tools. Journaled as `context.built` (records written before 0.14.0 have no `budgetTokens`); the full request is journaled beside it as `request.prepared`.

bus.name: assistant.message
bus.description: Published by the step loop once per provider response, after its assistant content is durably recorded and before any of its tool handlers runs: the text, the reasoning, the model, the tool calls, the token usage (input with its cache reads and writes inside, output with its reasoning inside) and why the response ended (`finishReason`: `stop`, `tool-calls` and `pause` are whole, `unknown` cuts a response only when it holds tool calls the loop would run, and any other reason cuts it; a cut one ran none of its tool calls, and its step ends `truncated`). A host-planned step 0 carries zero usage. Journaled only as `step.usage` (step, run, model, usage, finish reason): the content itself is memory's `memory.message`.

bus.name: stream.fallback
bus.description: Published by the step loop when a streamed provider call fails before its first part: the step is answered by a non-streamed call instead, and so is every later step of the run. Once per run at most. `message` is the stream's error as text, cut to 300 characters; it can quote the provider's error. A stream that fails after its first part fails the step instead (its tools may have run). A refusal over an image (an `InvalidRequestError` that names one) is no stream failure: it has no fallback; the turn omits the images and sends the step again (`StepRequest.onMediaRejected`), or the step fails. Journaled as `stream.fallback`.

bus.name: turn.ended
bus.description: Published once when the turn's reply is recorded (`TurnMemory.persistReply`, from `guardTurn`), also when the turn fails, with outcome failed; `usage` is the turn's usage, the usage of its `assistant.message` events summed (`RunContext.usage`). Under `Agent.turn` it is published after `use`, the host's per-turn layer and the turn-dependent plugins have closed, and their subscriptions with them: only a subscription whose scope is still open sees it, such as one made with `Scope.provide(observerScope)` over the caller's outer scope, or one registered around `TurnLive` by a host composing the turn itself. Otherwise read the `TurnResult` `Agent.turn` returns (its `usage` is the same total), or the stored `turn.reply` and `turn.ended`, and `turnUsageOf` over the stored events. Not journaled from the bus: memory stores `turn.reply` and the session its own `turn.ended` (reason and failure, no usage), both in the turn's closing commit, after its reactions: a reaction that fails fails the turn, its stored reply then failed (this event is not published again).

beginCodes.meaning: An attachment of the user's message is not an image the framework takes (not base64, not a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, over the size or pixel limits, too large together; see `MEDIA_LIMITS`). `Agent.turn` checks before it calls `Sessions.begin`: nothing was opened. The `HarnessError` carries the reason only in its message; a host that wants it typed (to answer 413 for `TooLarge` and `TooLargeTogether`, or name the attachment by its `index`) runs `normalizeUserMessage` from `@xandreed/core` on the message first and branches on `AttachmentRejected.reason`.
Another turn is open in the session. Retry after it ends, or queue the message.

beginCodes.http: 200 once that turn ended, 409 while it is open
beginCodes.meaning: The key was begun before with the same message, command and `resumes`: that turn is the answer, so serve its result instead of running again (`Sessions.lookup(address, key)` finds it).
The key was begun before with another message, command or `resumes` (the key `resume:<n>` begun again without `resumes` conflicts).

The run id was used before, by an earlier turn of the session or of the history a fork inherits: a run id names one turn's run (memory numbers its entries from it). Begin again with a new run id, a retry under a new key included; nothing was opened.
An inbox turn found nothing to take (inbox turns only).

The turn named in `resumes` cannot be resumed: `missing` (no such turn in the session, or `resumes` is not a whole number of at least 1), `inbox` (an inbox turn), `task` (a background task's turn), `superseded` (a user's turn began after it, other than a resume of it that failed, was cancelled or was interrupted) or `finished` (it ended completed, partial or failed). Only the last user's turn, ended cancelled or interrupted, can be; a resume that failed is tried again with a new key (and, as every turn, a new run id).

beginCodes.http: 429 for a quota or rate, 403 when not allowed, 503 while draining before a shutdown
beginCodes.meaning: The host's `TurnAdmission` refused the turn; nothing was opened or counted.
No such session for this owner.
Other writers kept committing to the session first, and nothing was opened. Retry later.
The session store failed. Retry later.

errorCodes.meaning: No configured image conversion tool is available through Bash. Install ImageMagick, libvips or sips, or provide another ImageResizer adapter.

errorCodes.where: `Agent.turn`, the turn writer (`TurnClosed`); a run started after the reply (`TurnMemory.startRun`)
errorCodes.meaning: The turn takes no more writes: someone else closed it (`cancelled`; `interrupted`, reaped; `removed`, its session removed), or it `ended` (its own end stored or under way, or its scope closed). The writer and `Agent.turn` fail with `TurnClosed`, whose `reason` says which; this is the code it stands for. A run of the step loop started once the turn's reply is recorded fails with a `HarnessError` of this code: the reply ends the turn's runs.

The turn failed with an error `harnessCodeOf` gives no code for (a tagged error without a `code`, or an untagged value, even one carrying a `code` such as a Node error's); the message is `<_tag>: <message>`, or the error as text (reason failed).

The turn died with a defect, an unexpected error; the message is the defect as text (reason failed). `Agent.turn` and `Sessions.drain` first turn a `TurnError` carried as a defect (a `HarnessError`, `TurnClosed`, ...) back into a failure, so it keeps its own code; a runner calling `turnEndingOf` itself does the same with `harnessDefectsAsFailures`.
The turn was interrupted before it ended: its body (`turnEndingOf`), the scope its writer lived in, or its begin after the opening commit (reason interrupted).

The turn's scope closed, without an interruption, before anyone tried to end the turn (reason failed). An end that was tried but could not be stored is tried again by the scope with that same ending, and a turn that held a completed or partial reply ends as that reply implies, not with this code.
The turn's holder stopped writing and another instance reaped it (reason interrupted).

errorCodes.where: a run of the step loop (`turn.run`, `runTurnLoop`)
errorCodes.meaning: The run's `budgetTokens` (the policy's, else the agent's) is not an integer of at least 1.
The agent's `budgetTokens` is not an integer of at least 1.
Memory was asked to record, for the turn's number or to start a run, before the user's message was taken.
The user's message was taken twice in one turn.
Memory numbered the user's message differently from the turn the session stored.

errorCodes.where: publishing a host event; a turn writer's `append` or `transact` and `Sessions.transact` (`ReservedKind`)
errorCodes.meaning: The host event's name, or the draft's kind, is one of the reserved kinds; only the framework's turn writes those (`frameworkDraft`).
Reactions nested deeper than `maxEventDepth` (8 by default).
A background handler was interrupted; the turn fails when the bus drains. One that dies with a defect fails it with that defect (`turn.defect`).

errorCodes.where: a host event's `make` / `publish`; the turn storing a bus event
errorCodes.meaning: The payload did not encode with the host event's schema, or its encoded form held a value JSON cannot (a BigInt), or a bus event did not encode with its own when the turn stored it (a value its type allows but a check refuses, such as a non-integer step).
A service the turn needs is not provided by the agent's plugins or the turn's services.

The plugin graph cannot be built (a missing provider, a cycle, a misplaced turn-dependent plugin), or the agent's turns would have no `ConversationMemory`, `ToolRegistry` or `StepLoop` (none from a plugin, `services` or `turnServices`).
The configuration still carries `profile` or `profiles`, which the graph does not resolve: fold the selected profile's plugins, bindings and system into the configuration first.
A plugin's options did not decode with its schema.

errorCodes.where: activating a plugin (a session plugin's, every turn)
errorCodes.meaning: The plugin's layer failed to build with an error that is not a `HarnessError` (one that is keeps its own code: `skills.duplicate`, `skills.root`, ...).

errorCodes.where: activating a plugin (a session plugin's, every turn)
errorCodes.meaning: The plugin's layer died with a defect that is not a `HarnessError` while it was built (one that is keeps its own code).

errorCodes.where: activating a plugin (`definePlugin`'s `build`); opening a run's tools (`ToolRegistry.open`); rendering a prompt section (`definePromptSection`)
errorCodes.meaning: A service the plugin lists in `requires`, or a tool or a prompt section in its own (`defineTool`, `definePromptSection`), is not among the services there; the message names the plugin, each tool or the section, and each missing service. The plugin's layer is not built; the run's tools do not open, so the turn fails before its first step (a handler called without one fails the call); the section does not render, so the turn fails where it renders the system prompt or its turn sections.
A replaceable module was used or replaced after its scope closed.
Two capabilities define a tool of the same name.
Two capabilities define a skill with the same id (a host's and a skills directory's: set the directory's `idPrefix`).
A skill names a tool no capability registers.
A skills tree has an issue: a `SKILL.md` without frontmatter or description, an id already used, a reference over the size limit. The message names each file.
A `required` skills root does not exist, or a root or a file in it cannot be read.
A skills root holds more files (`maxFiles`) or text (`maxBytes`) than allowed, or the roots more skills than `maxSkills`.
No skill of the catalog has that id. `load_skill` returns the refusal to the model as its failure, named `UnknownSkill`, and the turn goes on.

A tool of the selection needs a permission the turn was not granted. `load_skill` returns the refusal to the model as its failure, named `PermissionDenied`, and the turn goes on; a matcher's choice it refuses is not activated.
The selection names a skill or a tool the catalog does not hold, or the catalog holds two with one id.
The matcher did not answer within `matcherTimeoutMs`. The turn goes on: its decision is recorded as failed, and only the always-on skills are active.
The turn's tools were opened twice.
The tools were used before `openTurnTools` opened them.
The turn's services carry no `LanguageModel`.
The loop failed with an error that is not a `HarnessError` (the model call's own error, for example); the message is that error's message, without its tag (`messagesOf`), and the error is the cause.

errorCodes.where: the step loop, a run failing
errorCodes.meaning: The model's reply was cut short (its finish reason is not `stop`, `tool-calls` or `pause`; `unknown`, no finish reason given, cuts only a reply with tool calls the loop would run), and the run stops: a cut other than the output limit (`content-filter`, `error`, `other`, `unknown`), or more replies in a row cut at the output limit than the loop answers with correctives (2). The cut step is recorded, its status `truncated`, and none of its tool calls ran. `runLoop` fails with it as a `HarnessError`, and the step loop passes it on as it is.

errorCodes.where: the turn, before each provider call
errorCodes.meaning: The request header did not encode.
No stored `request.prepared` header for the step.
The step's stored `request.prepared` header did not decode.
The model's descriptor (provider, model and settings) did not decode.
The request about to be sent differs from the one rebuilt from its stored header and memory.
The selected model could not be resolved or described.
The memory events before a stored request did not decode.
Stored memory events did not decode, or memory could not be stored.
The digester's model call failed or did not answer within `digestTimeoutMs`. It is logged, and the turn goes on: memory records no digest, and the tool result stays whole.

The turn's services carry no `UtilityLlm`, and the turn fails when its memory opens; or the summarizer failed or did not answer within `summaryTimeoutMs`, which is logged: the turn goes on without a new summary, and its later steps do not ask again.

At a step, the system prompt and the active tools' schemas leave nothing of the context budget (`budgetTokens`); with the window strategy, also when the current turn alone does not fit the budget memory is given: the whole budget at the turn's start, what they leave at each step.

errorCodes.where: the turn writer, a turn failing with a `SessionLogError`
errorCodes.meaning: The session store failed during the turn. A turn that fails with a `SessionLogError` stores this code; the error's own `code` (`store.io`, ...) says what failed.

errorCodes.where: the turn writer, plugin-sessions' `Sessions` and the `Tasks` over it (`SessionContended`)
errorCodes.meaning: Too many conflicting writes to the session in a row: nothing was written, and a retry may succeed.
The input id already names another normalized message, delivery or source, or a legacy notice. Nothing was replaced or queued; retry with the original input or a new id.
The session's state, kept in its head, did not decode.

The writer's closing `turn.ended` did not encode. plugin-sessions' `Sessions` no longer raises it for a record or a state of its own since `SessionLogError` became storage only (it is a defect now); older journals may hold it.
A stored `turn.started` or `turn.ended` did not decode when the begin checked its key or the turn it resumes.

errorCodes.where: a stored `turn.ended` failure (reason `interrupted`), written by plugin-sessions' `Sessions` (`TurnShutdown.interrupt`)
errorCodes.meaning: The process shut down before the turn ended: the host's shutdown deadline passed (`shutdownGracefully`, `Agent.shutdown`, `AgentConfig.shutdown`) with the turn still running, and its end was stored while the log was still open. The turn is resumable, and its inbox items wait again with no attempt counted.

errorCodes.where: a stored `turn.ended` failure (reason `interrupted`), written by plugin-sessions' `Sessions`
errorCodes.meaning: The turn ran past its time limit (the begin's `timeLimitMs`, else the Sessions' `turns.timeLimitMs`): its holder closed it, and its writer refuses every later write with `TurnClosed` of reason `timed-out`. The turn is resumable; its inbox items wait again, an attempt counted.

errorCodes.where: a stored `turn.ended` failure (reason `interrupted`), written by plugin-sessions' `Sessions`
errorCodes.meaning: A begin with `takeOver` closed the session's open turn, still held by another holder, which the host says is gone (a restarted process). The turn is resumable, and its inbox items wait again with no attempt counted.

errorCodes.where: plugin-sessions' `Sessions` (a `SessionLogError`), before it plans a write
errorCodes.meaning: A newer release wrote the session: the stored format in its head (`STORED_FORMAT`) is above this release's. Nothing was written: `begin`, `deliver`, `drain`, `cancel`, `transact` and `fork` refuse it, while `get`, `list` and `read` still read it. Use that release or a later one.
Storing the turn's appended events died with a defect (a store or an encoder that threw); it is logged with its cause, and the writer refuses every later write and flush with this code.
The begin's opening commit came back uncommitted, or without the turn's `turn.started`. No longer raised since `SessionLogError` became storage only (it is a defect now); older journals may hold it.
The store answered the creation of a session without a parent with `SessionMissing`. No longer raised since `SessionLogError` became storage only (it is a defect now); older journals may hold it.
The store refused a commit made without a lease guard as expired (`LeaseExpired`). No longer raised since `SessionLogError` became storage only (it is a defect now); older journals may hold it.
The database file, or the store's directory, could not be created or opened; for the file store, also a directory without hard links, which it needs to publish a commit exclusively.
A read or a write failed, or a session just created could not be read back.
Another connection held the lock past the busy wait, or a new file could not be switched to WAL. Nothing was written, and a retry may succeed (`isStoreBusy`).
A stored row (a session's head or an event), or a commit file before a session's tail, did not decode.
A value to store (an event's data, the session's state or `meta`) is not one JSON can hold (a BigInt, a cycle).

A file system call did not answer within `stallMs` (a hung network mount), or the store is failing every call at once after such a stall, until one let through a `stallMs` later answers. A commit that stalled may still land: read the head again before deciding it did not.

A newer release wrote the store: the SQLite file's schema version (`PRAGMA user_version`), or the directory's layout (`store.json`), is above the last one this release knows. Nothing was read or written; open it with that release or a later one. A SQLite file without a version, as 0.14.0 wrote it, still opens.
A task's `task.started` or `task.result` did not encode. No longer raised since `SessionLogError` became storage only (it is a defect now); older journals may hold it.

The session refused one of the tasks plugin's records as a reserved kind (`ReservedKind`); its kinds are not reserved. No longer raised since `SessionLogError` became storage only (it is a defect now); older journals may hold it.
The task was started, but the parent session does not hold it when read back. No longer raised since `SessionLogError` became storage only (it is a defect now); older journals may hold it.
The store's data could not be read or decoded. Nothing was read as absent and nothing was written over it: fix or remove it.
The settings' data could not be read or decoded. Nothing was read as defaults and nothing was written over it: fix or remove it.

records.when: `Tasks.start`: the task's instructions, mode, the starter's `meta` and, when given, the turn that started it (`startedBy`); its child session is created with it.
Before the child's turn ends (or outside a turn when the host refused it): the outcome, reply and failure.
`Tasks.cancel`, while the task is pending or running; the first of a result and a cancellation ends the task.

codes.meaning: The task's turn failed, or died with an error that is not a `HarnessError` (a `HarnessError` keeps its own code).
The host would not admit the task's turn.

codes.where: a task's result or the parent's reaction
codes.meaning: The task runner's deadline cut the work.
The task's turn stopped without a result.
The task's session was removed with its parent.
